card.hook: Everything at Český Krumlov Castle is stacked up a long rocky hillside, so even a quick snap comes out with depth. Towers, bridges, courtyards and walls all pile on top of each other, and your phone will love it.
card.stand_here: Stand at the phone icon on the map, about 30 m west of the subject, and face east. Keep your phone level and let the castle fill the upper part of the frame.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the castle and its setting. If you're close and the walls and tower won't fit, drop to 0.5x. From a distance, try 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out the tower, the rooftops or the Cloak Bridge.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and put the tower on one of the vertical lines, then tap the castle walls and make the picture a touch darker if the sky is washing out.
card.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon gives you softer light and fewer people in your shot. Midday can be harsh and bright, so check how the light looks on the walls before you press the button.
card.selfie_here: Head to the Seminární zahrada (Seminary Garden) on Horní Street and sit on the red-tiled ledge of the terrace garden next to the Regional Museum. It's built for posing, so use the front camera at 0.5x with the castle and town filling the background behind you.
card.ask_someone: Stand at the end of the Lávka pod Zámkem footbridge, right under the Cloak Bridge, so the bridge and castle sit behind you, and ask a passer-by to shoot toward you.
card.rules_and_safety: The ledges along the castle wall near the Cloak Bridge are high, so mind your bag and phone when you pose there. The castle has ticketed areas as well as public parts, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Can you get all five storeys of the Cloak Bridge into one picture without chopping off the top?
card.good_to_know: The first castle here dates back to 1253, built by the Vítkovci family. It's been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1992 and is the second largest castle and chateau complex in the Czech Republic, after Prague Castle. The Cloak Bridge dates from 1764, and the Baroque theatre from 1767 is counted among the best preserved in the world. Right next to it: Castle Tower. Right next to it: Cloak Bridge (Plášťový most).
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the phone icon on the map, about 30 m west of the subject, and face east. Keep your phone level and let the castle fill the upper part of the frame.

card.hook: A pink spire pokes up between the neighbouring buildings like it's peeking over a fence, and it's hard not to grin at it. Use those buildings to frame the church.
card.stand_here: Stand at the phone icon on the map, about 35 m north-west of the Church of St. Vitus, and face south-east toward the church.
card.zoom: Start at 1x to get the church with its surroundings. Then try 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) for architectural details, instead of walking into the road. Only use 0.5x if you step closer and want the whole building in a tight space.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines and line the church walls up with the vertical lines, and hold the phone level so the building doesn't lean.
card.best_time: Soft morning or late-afternoon light usually flatters stonework. Early in the day is often calmer too.
card.selfie_here: Head to Kostelní Street (Kostelní ulice) and pose so the pink spire fills the gap between the narrow houses on either side. Use the front camera, and if you want more of the scene, try 0.5x. The Cloak Bridge corridors are another option, with the church visible from the walkway.
card.ask_someone: Ask someone to stand near the middle of the Dr. Edvard Beneš Bridge over the Vltava, so the spire and the whole church fit in the frame.
card.rules_and_safety: The church is a place of worship, so be respectful and check the official site before you go for visiting arrangements. On the Dr. Edvard Beneš Bridge the sidewalks have been closed by wooden barriers since 2018, so people walk in the road, though traffic is light.
card.challenge: Take one wide shot, then step in and find one stone detail to zoom in on. Bonus points if the verticals are dead straight.
card.good_to_know: The Church of St. Vitus is in Český Krumlov, and it's the second-ranked spot on our Český Krumlov map. It's a place of worship, so keep that in mind while you snap. If other visitors wander into your shot, wait a moment and take a few photos.

card.hook: Got rooftops and walls between you and the Castle Tower? Lucky you. Those buildings are your secret ingredient, because the tower looks best peeking out from behind them.
card.stand_here: Stand at the phone icon on the map, about 240 m south-east of the tower, and face north-west. Keep your phone upright and level so the walls don't lean.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to get the whole scene. Then try zoom 2x to 5x, depending on your phone, to pick out the top of the tower. It also makes the tower look closer to the buildings in front of it. Use zoom 0.5x only if you walk closer and need to fit in the full height.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the tower on one of the vertical lines, then tap the tower and slide it a little darker if the sky looks washed out.
card.best_time: Soft morning or late-afternoon light is kinder to the walls and sky than midday sun. Early in the day it's usually quieter too.
card.selfie_here: Stand in the cobbled Radniční Street at the end nearest Lazebnický most, where the castle tower sits at the far end of the street. Use the front camera, hold it a bit low and turn so the tower is over your shoulder. For a different look, try the corner of Masná and Horní streets, where the house façades frame the rounded tower.
card.ask_someone: If you'd like someone else to take your photo, the terrace of the Seminární zahrada (Seminary Garden) on Horní Street, next to the Regional Museum, has the castle and tower in view across the town.
card.rules_and_safety: The ledges along the castle wall are high, so take care setting up there and keep a firm grip on your phone. If you want to go up the tower or into the grounds, check the official site first, as access may be ticketed or restricted.
card.challenge: Take one wide shot with a building in the foreground and one zoomed shot of just the tower top, then see which one your friends 'like' more.
card.good_to_know: The Castle Tower is ranked third on the Český Krumlov map. Passers-by drift through the shot a lot, so take a few frames, or try Live Photos to pick the cleanest moment. If people or signs creep in, shift a step to one side instead of cropping later.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the phone icon on the map, about 240 m south-east of the tower, and face north-west. Keep your phone upright and level so the walls don't lean.

card.hook: Bridges are a bit of a cheat code for phone photos: strong lines, a clear sense of place, and no need to ask them to smile. Cloak Bridge, number 4 on the Český Krumlov map, does it all in a very compact town.
card.stand_here: Stand at the phone icon on the map, about 30 m north-west of the Cloak Bridge, and face south-east. Take your first photo from here before you move closer.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for a natural view of the whole bridge. If it won't all fit, try 0.5x, but don't overdo it because it can stretch the edges. Then go to 2x or more for a detail, and take a couple of frames at different zooms so you can keep the best later.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines and line the bridge up with a horizontal line so it doesn't look tilted.
card.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light and fewer people. Take a test shot on the day to check how the light looks.
card.selfie_here: Walk from the bridge toward the Castle Gardens, turn left to the viewing platform in the 5th courtyard just in front of the castle gate, and stand on the balcony corner with the bridge behind you. Use the front camera, try 0.5x, and get the castle and town in the background. For a different look, stand at the arched openings in the wall on your left and frame yourself against the town.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on the wooden Lávka pod Zámkem footbridge, where it reaches the Cloak Bridge, with the bridge straight ahead, while you pose in front of it.
card.rules_and_safety: Surfaces here may be uneven, so watch your footing while you look at your screen.
card.challenge: Wait for a gap in the crowd and grab one frame with the bridge empty, then one with a stranger crossing to show how big it is.
card.good_to_know: Cloak Bridge (Plášťový most) is number 4 on the Český Krumlov map. The town is so compact that the bridge fits easily into a wider scene of its surroundings. No access information is available for this spot, so check on the day.

card.hook: Grab a spot at the edge of Svornosti Square and let the buildings do the work: the rooflines and colourful façades make a ready-made frame, and there's nearly always someone strolling through the middle to add life.
card.stand_here: Stand at the phone icon on the map, about 40 m east of the subject in Svornosti Square, and face west. It's roughly a minute's walk, so you can try a few spots without going far.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit the whole square and the buildings around it, then switch to 1x for a more natural look. Try 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out façade details or people on the far side.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and line up the building edges with the vertical lines so nothing leans, then tap the brightest part of the buildings and drag the slider a touch darker to keep the sky and light façades from washing out.
card.best_time: Early morning or later in the evening usually means fewer people in the frame and softer light on the façades. An overcast day works nicely here too, so check the sky on the day.
card.selfie_here: Head to the middle of Svornosti Square, by the hexagonal fountain around the Plague Column. Use the front camera at 0.5x, hold your phone a little higher, and let the column and the colourful Renaissance houses fill in behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: It's an outdoor public square, but check local event information before you go in case of events or restrictions.
card.challenge: Find a lamp, a bench or the edge of a building and use it in the bottom corner of your shot, then see if you can get a clean frame with no strangers in it (good luck, it's a busy square).
card.good_to_know: Svornosti Square is a town square in Český Krumlov. The fountain and Plague Column sit at its centre, with colourful Renaissance houses around them. Busy squares change from minute to minute, so check each shot and take a few at different heights.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the phone icon on the map, about 40 m east of the subject in Svornosti Square, and face west. It's roughly a minute's walk, so you can try a few spots without going far.

card.hook: Rooftops, tall façades and a road that pulls your eye straight down the middle: Latrán street is a ready-made picture before you've even raised your phone. It's number 6 on the Český Krumlov map.

card.zoom: Start at 1x to catch the whole street and its surroundings. Then try 2x or more to squeeze the buildings together and fill the frame with the street. Take both: the wide one shows where you were, the close one shows the detail.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and line up the road or rooflines with them so the walls stay nice and straight.
card.best_time: Soft morning or late-afternoon light usually flatters the façades, and earlier in the day is often quieter. Check which way the light falls on the day, because the street may be in shade at some times.
card.selfie_here: Try the small park just behind the city theatre, where the castle, the river and the Latrán district all show up together. Use the front camera at 0.5x and hold it low so the view sits over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Try the bridge where Latrán street crosses the Polečnice stream: you stand on the bridge, and ask a passer-by to step back along the street and take your picture with Latrán behind you.
card.challenge: Shoot one wide 1x picture and one 2x close-up of the same stretch, then see which one you'd actually send to your friends.
card.good_to_know: Latrán street is number 6 on the Český Krumlov map. Budějovická Gate (Budějovice Gate) marks the far end of Latrán. It's the only one of the town's nine original gates still standing.

card.hook: Picture a row of stone arches with the castle buildings and a sea of red roofs tucked in behind them. That's the Castle Gardens view, and you get it before you even step into the garden.

card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to fit the arcaded bridge with the castle and red roofs behind it. Tap 0.5x if you want more of the garden entrance in the shot. Try 2x or higher (depends on your phone) to pick out roofs and castle details through the arches.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on your gridlines and line the bridge arches up with the vertical lines so the arcade looks nice and straight.
card.best_time: Go when the garden is open, because the hours change with the season. Check before you head over.
card.selfie_here: Try the small garden between the Cloak Bridge and the Castle Garden entrance, which one reviewer calls the best view point in town. Use the front camera at 0.5x and keep the castle and bridge over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by near the entrance to the Castle Gardens, where the Old Town and the castle both come into view, to take your photo.
card.rules_and_safety: Photography is generally allowed in the gardens, but don't block the paths. Take care along the castle wall west of the Cloak Bridge, because the ledges of the stone window openings there are high.
card.challenge: Get the arches dead straight on the gridlines, then snap a second shot with you grinning in front of them.
card.good_to_know: The Castle Gardens are part of the castle complex, reached over the Cloak Bridge. Guides call the bridge one of the most typical Krumlov views. Walking across the outside is free, but the bridge interior is only on the guided castle tour.

card.hook: Everyone's eyes go straight to the castle, and fair enough. Now look just to its right, where a garden and a brewery are tucked in among the houses. That's the monastery, the quiet one in the picture.
card.stand_here: Stand in Seminární zahrada, about 290 m south-west of the subject, and face north-east. The Vltava is between you and the castle, and the monastery is among the houses to the right of it.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to get the castle, river and rooftops all in one go. Then try 1x for a cleaner look at the garden and brewery, and 2x to pick out the monastery beside the castle.

card.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon usually means softer light and fewer people. The view works any time of day, though, and the light changes with the season.
card.selfie_here: Switch to the front camera, try zoom 0.5x so more of the scene fits in, and hold the phone a little high. Turn so the town is over your shoulder and take a few, because the first one is always mostly forehead.
card.rules_and_safety: Seminární zahrada is a public park, but the monastery and its garden aren't part of the viewpoint. If you want to go inside, check the official site first.
card.challenge: Take one wide shot of the whole scene, then one tight shot of just the monastery corner, and see if a friend can guess it's the same view.
card.good_to_know: The monastery is a good example of Český Krumlov's layered skyline. Its garden and brewery rise among the houses to the right of the castle. One frame shows the castle complex, the river, the Old Town rooftops and the monastery together.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Seminární zahrada, about 290 m south-west of the subject, and face north-east. The Vltava is between you and the castle, and the monastery is among the houses to the right of it.

selfie_spots.name: Tramín courtyard, behind the Baroque gate from Klášterní Street
selfie_spots.detail: in the courtyard just inside the Baroque gate on Klášterní Street (Latrán no. 50)
selfie_spots.why: The courtyard is the entry point to the monastery area and is surrounded by the church and monastery buildings, so a visitor standing there may have the complex behind them; no page confirms this framing.

sources.title: Gardens of the Former Minorite monastery in Český Krumlov (ckrumlov.cz encyclopedia)

selfie_research.notes: The sources I found do not name a spot where the visitor has the Minorite Monastery behind them, nor a spot where a passer-by can frame the whole monastery. The Tramín courtyard is the only named place that is close to that, and the photo framing is my inference, not a page's claim. Access conflicts: the ckrumlov.cz encyclopedia says the monastery area is inaccessible at present and that the courtyard will open after reconstruction, while ckrumlov.info says the town opened the complex to the public in 2015, and a Nomads guide lists hours of Tuesday to Sunday 10:30–18:00 at Klášterní Dvůr 97. Check current access before going. Photography inside is generally allowed, but some exhibition areas may restrict it (airial.travel). No page I found mentions selfie stick or tripod rules.

card.hook: Plant your feet at the phone icon and you get a small luxury: room to shoot the whole scene, then a tighter one, without moving an inch. Take your time here, because this view rewards a few extra frames.
card.stand_here: Stand about 170 m east of the subject, at the phone icon on the map, and face west toward the Seminary Garden viewpoint.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for the whole scene. Then try 0.5x for a more open view, and 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out details in the distance.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on gridlines, keep the horizon level, and put the main part of the view on a line instead of dead centre, with a few leaves or a bit of railing peeking in at the edge for depth.
card.best_time: Soft light in the morning or late afternoon usually flatters a view like this. Pick a time when the part you want to photograph is lit and not in shadow.
card.selfie_here: Head to the red-tiled ledge inside the Seminary Garden terrace and stand with the town and castle behind you. Use the front camera, try 0.5x to fit more in, and keep the landmark over your shoulder.
card.rules_and_safety: Check access and any opening arrangements for the garden on the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Take one wide shot and one close one from the same spot, then see which one you'd actually send to your friends.
card.good_to_know: The Seminary Garden viewpoint is a stop on the Český Krumlov map. The phone icon is about 170 m east of the subject. That gap lets you take a scene-setting shot and a closer one without walking anywhere.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand about 170 m east of the subject, at the phone icon on the map, and face west toward the Seminary Garden viewpoint.

selfie_spots.name: Seminární zahrada (Seminary Garden), red-tiled ledge
selfie_spots.detail: on the red-tiled ledge inside the garden terrace, with the town and castle behind you
selfie_spots.why: Guides describe this ledge as built for posing, with the whole town as the backdrop, and it is the most-cited photo spot in the garden.

card.hook: Here's a Český Krumlov photo that isn't the usual town view: just a street, a building and a few people wandering past.
card.stand_here: Stand about 150 m north of the subject, at the phone icon on the map near Egon Schiele Art Centrum and Široká, and face south.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for a natural look at the front of the building. If you can't step back, try 0.5x, but keep the building near the middle so the edges don't stretch. Zoom 2x gets you a tighter shot without stepping into the road.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and line up the building's edges with them so the walls stand straight.
card.best_time: Early morning or later in the day should be best, with fewer people on the street and softer light.
card.selfie_here: Try the leafy courtyard of the Egon Schiele Art Centrum (Široká 71), where a travel guide points to the historic walls and sculpture installations as a standout backdrop. Use the front camera, switch to zoom 0.5x if you want more in, and keep the walls or a sculpture over your shoulder.
card.rules_and_safety: Check the official site before you go for visiting rules, and don't go inside to photograph the artworks without checking first.
card.challenge: Get one frame where the building stands perfectly straight on the gridlines, with a little street in front and a strip of sky above it.
card.good_to_know: The Egon Schiele Art Centrum is a museum and gallery devoted to the Austrian painter Egon Schiele. It was set up in 1992 by a group of Czechs, Austrians and Americans. Since 1993 it has shown a permanent Schiele exhibition, plus yearly displays of 20th-century art by names like Picasso, Dalí and Klimt.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand about 150 m north of the subject, at the phone icon on the map near Egon Schiele Art Centrum and Široká, and face south.

selfie_spots.detail: in the museum's leafy courtyard, inside the gallery complex on Široká
selfie_spots.why: A travel guide suggests the courtyard for a standout shot, pointing to the historic walls and sculpture installations there.

selfie_spots.detail: on Široká Street, close to Náměstí Svornosti (the main square)
selfie_spots.why: One blogger describes a cobbled pavement on this street that felt like an arrow pointing toward the buildings in the distance.

The Široká entry is a generic street tip: the blog does not say the gallery appears in its frame, and the photo has no confirmed link to the gallery. The courtyard tip comes from a travel-guide aggregator page, not an official source. A Wikimedia Commons category lists views 'towards Egon Schiele Museum' on Široká, but it gives no standing point, so I did not use it. The same Trip.com guide's 'lawn behind the Regional Museum' is a different place and was excluded. No page I found states rules about selfie sticks or tripods for this site, and none mentions a safety point.

card.hook: Here's a little Český Krumlov trick: one view gives you a street, a river and a jumble of old-town rooftops, no wandering required. The Vltava does half the work by drawing a line straight through your photo.
card.stand_here: Head to where Linecká street meets the Vltava and stand about 15 m north-west of the subject, at the phone icon on the map. Face south-east.
card.zoom: Start at 1x, which looks natural and works for most shots. If the pavement is narrow, tap 0.5x to fit street, water and sky together, but keep people and signs away from the edges, where things get stretched. For a single roofline or a reflection on the water, try 2x or higher (depends on your phone).
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and line the river up with one so it doesn't tilt, then tap the brightest part of the picture and drag it a touch darker so the sky keeps its colour.
card.best_time: Early morning or early evening is usually calmer, with softer light. At dusk, switch on night mode and rest your elbows on something firm to keep the phone steady.
card.selfie_here: Try the steps down to the Vltava at the far end of the Town Park, near the little wooden platform reaching into the water. A blogger describes it as a river-level view with St. Vitus Church across the water, so use the front camera, hold it a bit low and let the church sit over your shoulder. Or climb to the top of the Plešivec steps on Plešivecké náměstí for a view of the town, which a guide says shows St. Vitus Church well. Neither spot is confirmed to have Linecká street in the shot, so think of these as town-view selfies.
card.ask_someone: Stand in the open area in front of the Linecká school (Základní škola Linecká), with the Plešivec steps and the street behind you, and ask a passer-by to take your photo from a few steps away.
card.rules_and_safety: Stay aware of traffic and other walkers. It's an ordinary street by the river, but check the official site before you go if you plan to enter any nearby attraction.
card.challenge: Find one rooftop reflection wobbling in the water, then see if you can snap it before a duck, a boat or a passing tourist ruins it.
card.good_to_know: This is the spot where Linecká street meets the Vltava in Český Krumlov. The river gives you a natural line to lead the eye, and the street adds the look of the old town. Check the water's edge before you press the button, because railings and signs love to sneak into the frame.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Head to where Linecká street meets the Vltava and stand about 15 m north-west of the subject, at the phone icon on the map. Face south-east.

selfie_spots.detail: at the top of the Plešivec stairs, on Plešivecké náměstí square, reached by climbing from the area in front of the Linecká schoolhouse
selfie_spots.why: The square gives a view of the town from its southern side, and a guide says it shows the St. Vitus Church well, though the page does not say Linecká street is in frame.

selfie_research.notes: Weak evidence: no page found names a selfie spot where Linecká street or its Vltava bridge is directly behind the visitor. Both selfie spots are town and river views, not street views. The ask-someone spot is a named starting point from which the guide route climbs the steps; the page does not say the school front gives a framed shot of the whole street, so the framing in the detail is my inference. The Wikimedia Commons category lists a bridge of Linecká street over the Vltava and a photo titled as a view on the 'Bridge Saint Jan Nepomuk', but I found no page describing that bridge as a selfie or photo spot. The given coordinates (48.80876, 14.31568) sit very close to Linecká 46, the camera location of a Commons photo, but that is only a metadata point, not a recommendation. No selfie-stick, tripod or safety rule was found on any page I read.

card.hook: Most people walk onto Barber's Bridge and photograph the view from it. Try the opposite: walk down Latrán and watch the bridge close off the end of the street, with the castle rising right behind it.
card.stand_here: Stand on Latrán at the Spičák end about 150 m north-east of the bridge. Face south-west and the bridge is a short walk ahead of you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x so the bridge, the street edges and the castle all fit. If the street is busy and you can't step back, tap 0.5x. If your phone has 2x or 5x, try that to bring the bridge and castle in tighter.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the bridge on the centre line, and let the buildings on both sides frame it while you keep your phone level so the street doesn't lean.
card.best_time: Early morning or later in the evening is likely to mean fewer people in the street, so the bridge is easier to frame cleanly. Whenever you go, take a few frames as people walk through and keep the one with the clearest view.
card.selfie_here: Flip to the front camera and try 0.5x so more of the scene fits in behind you. Turn so the bridge or castle sits over your shoulder, and take a few in case someone wanders into the shot.
card.rules_and_safety: The bridge has been closed for reconstruction in the past, so check it's open before you plan your walk.
card.challenge: Take one shot where the street edges frame the bridge perfectly straight, then see if you can get one with no strangers in it.
card.good_to_know: Barber's Bridge (Lazebnický most) crosses the river in the old part of Český Krumlov. Guides describe Latrán as the main walking route to it. For a second picture, walk onto the bridge for the castle and river view, though the bridge itself won't be in that shot.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Latrán at the Spičák end, at the phone icon on the map, about 150 m north-east of the bridge. Face south-west and the bridge is a short walk ahead of you.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a spot where a visitor can stand with Barber's Bridge (Lazebnický most) behind them, or a spot where a passer-by can frame a visitor with the whole bridge in view. Most pages describe the bridge as a viewpoint over the Vltava toward the castle, not as a backdrop for a selfie. The Tripadvisor listing for the Laibon restaurant (Parkán 105) carries a photo titled 'View of the castle and barber's bridge', but the page does not say where that photo was taken or where anyone should stand, so I did not use it. Two Český Krumlov selfie spots I found, the Cloak Bridge and the castle viewpoint behind the wooden door at the end of the fortification wall, are different places from Barber's Bridge and are not included. No page states any rule about selfie sticks or tripods for this bridge; one 360° panorama page says its photographer put a tripod on a wooden beam outside the bridge, but that is a description of one shoot, not a rule. No safety point about this bridge is stated. Sources checked: czechtravellers.com, know-your-destination.com, trip.com, wanderlog.com, 360cities.net, Flickr (dgmckelvey), Wikimedia Commons, Tripadvisor, prague itinerary, chrisandwrensworld.com, thirdeyetraveller.com, worldwanderings.net, robgreebonphotography.com.

card.hook: Picture a raft full of people lining up for the wide gap in a weir, and you're standing right above them with your phone out. That's the Jez U Jelení lávky, just below Český Krumlov castle, and the rafts shooting through make a lively show.
card.stand_here: Stand about 640 m north of the subject, on Jelení lávka, and face south. You'll be on the footbridge over the weir, looking down at the wide sluice.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x so the weir, the river and the raft all fit. Try 2x-5x (depends on your phone) to pick out one raft and its paddlers, or 0.5x for the whole weir with the castle above, though the boats will look small.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the water right where the raft will come through, so your phone is ready before it arrives.
card.best_time: Go in the daytime between May and September, when rafting trips generally run. If the water looks empty, wait a few minutes.
card.selfie_here: Try the small footbridge just downstream of the weir, below the castle. Use the front camera at 0.5x and keep the weir and the castle behind your shoulder.
card.rules_and_safety: The footbridge is a public crossing with no charge noted. Rafting trips between Český Krumlov and Zlatá Koruna suit children who wear life jackets.
card.challenge: Take a burst of shots as each raft passes and see if you can catch the moment it drops through the sluice with the paddles up.
card.good_to_know: This weir on the Vltava is known as Jez U Jelení lávky. Rafts and canoes run down the river through its wide sluice. Rafting trips on the river generally run from May to September.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand about 640 m north of the subject, on Jelení lávka (the phone icon on the map), and face south. You'll be on the footbridge over the weir, looking down at the wide sluice.
